its holders become `admin`. A `team_lead` ranks below `admin`, so
nothing an admin-only endpoint guards is open to one.

CapabilityValue.description:
A matrix cell's value: a switch is `off`/`on`; a visibility row takes
the levels its `values` list — nothing, the chats the person is
assigned to or has joined, their teams', the whole workspace.

CapabilityValues.description:
Every capability's resolved value, by key (`chats.view` → `team`). What
a capability with no scope of its own — `chats.view`'s `own` level, or
seeing a player's email and username (`customers.contact.view`) — is
checked against.

priority.description:
Queue priority. Higher is more urgent; 0 is the
default. Bounded to [-100, 100].

customer_name.description: Null for a visitor who never introduced themselves.

customer_email.description: Null when the caller's role may not see a player's contact details (`customers.contact.view`).

customer_has_email.description:
Whether the customer left an address — whether a status change can
e-mail them (`email_template_id`). True also when `customer_email`
is masked.

source_chat_id.description: The conversation this followed on from, if any.

source_thread_id.description:
The connection the ticket was opened from — the chat's newest when
it was created (`source_chat_id` is the member's day, this is one
connection inside it). Null off a chat, and on tickets created before
it was recorded. Panelde: Chat ID (bağlantı); `source_chat_id` is
Panelde: Thread ID (günlük).

merged_into_id.description:
The primary ticket this one is folded into, or null
when it stands alone. A merged ticket is hidden from the lists.

related_ticket_id.description:
The earlier ticket this one follows on from: the
player answered a ticket that was closed, or quiet longer than the
workspace's reopen window (`ticket_reopen_window_days`), so the
answer opened this one instead of reopening that one. Null otherwise.

source_chat.description:
A snapshot of the conversation the ticket came from, so an agent
picking the ticket up has the context without hunting for it.

followers.description: Agents watching this ticket without owning it.

merged_ticket_ids.description: Ids of the tickets merged into this one (empty unless it is a primary).

tags.description: Tag names on the ticket — what a ticket rule's "add tag" writes.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields defined for tickets, with this ticket's values.

TicketMessageAttachment.description:
One file on a ticket message. `key` is the storage key — an
upload's (`POST /uploads`) on a reply or note, a file the player
e-mailed on their message (tm 357, served only through
`GET /tickets/{ticketId}/messages/{messageId}/attachments/{attachmentKey}`).
Only a `clean` file is offered for download or mailed. A `sensitive`
file (an ID document, a bank statement) is drawn behind a click, and
`locked` when the caller's role may not open it.

purged.description:
The bytes were deleted under the workspace's conversation retention
window — a sensitive file goes when the window does. The entry
stays so the thread still says a file was there.

locked.description:
Set on a read, for this caller: the file is sensitive and their
role does not hold `customers.documents.view`, so the download
refuses it.

TicketMessage.description:
One entry in a ticket's conversation, oldest first in
`GET /tickets/{ticketId}/messages`.

- `customer_message` — what the player wrote (an inbound e-mail, the
  ticket's opening text).
- `agent_reply` — an agent's answer, sent to the player by e-mail;
  `delivery_status` says where that e-mail is.
- `internal_note` — for the team only. Never e-mailed and never shown
  to the player; `delivery_status` is always null on it.
- `system` — a line the product wrote (a merge, a reopening).

`ticket_id` is the ticket the message was written on: a primary's
thread also shows the messages of the tickets merged into it, and this
says which one each came from.

author_id.description: The agent's account for `agent`, the customer for `customer`; null for `system` and `bot`.

author_name.description: The agent's or the player's name as it reads now; null when there is none.

body_text.description:
The text, with card numbers masked. A reply or note is at most
20 000 characters. On an inbound e-mail it is what the player
wrote this time — the quoted earlier mail and the signature cut —
at most 100 000 characters.

body_text_full.description:
Only on a `customer_message` from e-mail, and only when something
was cut from `body_text`: the whole text as it arrived (masked
alike), for "show full message" — cutting a quote is a guess, so
the original is kept beside it.

body_html.description:
Only on a `customer_message` that arrived as HTML, and only after
sanitising at intake against an allow list. Still not markup to
put in a page: the console draws `body_text`, and offers this as
"formatted view" in a frame with an empty `sandbox` and a CSP that
loads nothing.

delivery_status.description:
Only on an `agent_reply`. `queued` — saved, the e-mail goes after
the commit · `sent` — the mail server took it · `failed` — it did
not; the console offers "try again" · `suppressed` — this
deployment keeps ticket e-mail off, the reply is kept and the
thread says it was not sent.

sender_mismatch.description:
Present, and true, on a `customer_message` that reached the ticket
from an address other than its player's: a reply address or
a thread reference matched, the sender did not. The message is
kept; the console warns before anyone acts on it.

TicketMessageInput.description:
What the composer sends. `kind: reply` goes to the player by
e-mail; `kind: note` stays with the team and never reaches the mail
path. `idempotency_key` makes a retried request one message: the same
key on the same licence answers with the message already stored.

attachment_keys.description: Storage keys of files uploaded through `POST /uploads` for this licence.

set_status.description:
"Send and …": the status the ticket moves to in the same request.
Without it a reply leaves the ticket `pending` (waiting on the
player) and a note leaves the status as it was.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields defined for contacts, with this contact's values.

visits_count.description:
The true total, unlike `visits` below which is capped at the
most recent entries — a returning visitor's real count cannot
be read from the truncated array.

groups.description: Teams this visitor's conversations have been routed to, deduplicated. Empty for a visitor with no chats.

connections.description:
The day's connections (`threads`), oldest first, newest 20 at most —
the profile reads "day → connection". `id` above is the day
(Panelde: Thread ID, günlük); each connection's `id` here is
Panelde: Chat ID (bağlantı).

came_from.description: Referring URL, when the browser sent one.

pages.description: Pages seen during the visit, in order.

public_name.description:
What visitors see in the widget instead of `name`, set by
the person on "My profile". `null` means `name` is shown.

concurrent_chats_limit.description: Routing never assigns past this. Over-limit means queued.

last_seen_at.description:
When this person was last active anywhere in SiyahTuş, coarsened to the
minute. Account-wide by design — `accounts` is a
person, not a membership, so someone who works two workspaces
carries one timestamp across both. `null` means never seen since the
column started being written.

Not the same thing as presence: presence is a live socket and
disappears when the tab closes, this is a durable stamp. And not the
per-licence "last sign-in" the access-review report answers with — that one is read off the audit trail precisely because it
has to be about *this* workspace.

suspended.description:
A suspended agent is reachable through this list (with
`status=suspended` or `status=all`) but cannot be assigned work and
does not occupy a billed seat.

expertise.description:
The expertise areas assigned to this agent (FR-MOD-08.6.3 —
skill-based routing), ordered by name. Empty when none are set. Set
wholesale through `PUT /agents/{agentId}/expertise`.

Expertise.description:
An area of expertise a licence defines for skill-based routing. Called "expertise" at the data layer because "skills" is
the AI-automation concept; the product surface may still label it a skill.

slug.description: Derived from the name, unique within the licence.

QueueTopicRole.description:
A team queue's topic (AU-01 · K14 · `@siyahtus/types`
`QUEUE_TOPIC_ROLES`). The AI's hand-over, the pre-chat topic and a
hand-over rule's `{ topic }` target resolve the role, not the team's
name, so a renamed team still receives its topic.
`responsible_gambling` has rules of its own: no fallback
team, only trained agents, and the team cannot be deleted.

AfterHoursMode.description:
What a team's queue does when nobody is on shift (AU-01;
`@siyahtus/types` `AFTER_HOURS_MODES`): `queue` — the conversation
waits for the next agent; `ticket` — it becomes a ticket the player
is answered on by email (HD-01 / WG-08).

GroupAssignmentMode.description:
How a team's conversations reach its agents (WG-07 · `@siyahtus/types`
`GROUP_ASSIGNMENT_MODES`): `auto` — routing picks the agent (tier,
load, longest idle); `manual` — routing picks nobody: the
conversation waits in the team's queue, every member is told
(`incoming_chat`), and the first to take it
(`POST /chats/{chatId}/claim`) has it, within their concurrent limit.
With the workspace's unanswered window set, a conversation nobody has
taken for that long is reported to the team's leads
(`chat_unanswered_alert`, reason `unclaimed`) instead of being
passed on.

ThreadPriority.description:
How pressing a connection is (ADR-08a · AI-12; `@siyahtus/types`
`THREAD_PRIORITIES`): `urgent` — self-harm, a suspected minor, a
self-exclusion request; `high` — a repeat contact the same day, an
angry player; `normal` — the rest. A team's queue serves the most
pressing first, then the longest waiting. Stored as a rank
(`threads.priority`), so it never sorts by spelling.

accepting_count.description:
How many of the team's members are accepting chats right now —
not suspended, not awaiting approval — whatever their load (IN-04:
"Finance · 2 online" in the hand-off menu).

topic_role.description: The topic this team's queue is for; null for an ordinary team.

required_expertise_ids.description:
Expertise areas an agent must hold — all of them — to be given this
team's conversations, in ascending id order. Empty: none.

priority.description:
Assignment preference within the team. A full tier is
skipped rather than queued behind.

lead.description:
Whether this member leads the team (RL-01,
`group_agents.is_lead`). A lead is a member too: they are
offered the team's chats like anyone in it.

message.description: Human-readable; never contains secrets or raw SQL.

request_id.description: Correlates with server logs and traces.

PageId.name: page_id
PageId.description: Opaque keyset cursor from the previous page.

ChatId.name: chatId
ChatId.description: Short base32 chat token. Panelde: Thread ID (günlük).

BrandHeader.name: X-SiyahTus-Brand
BrandHeader.description:
Scope the request to one brand of the caller's license (Multibrand,
PRD §5.3 · NFR-S4). Omitted means every brand of the license — the
single-brand default, so a workspace that never uses Multibrand is
unaffected. A brand id that is not one of the caller's own is answered
404, never 403, so brand ids stay un-enumerable across licenses.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, malformed or expired credentials. When the bearer credential
itself was refused — expired, revoked or never issued, the three told
apart nowhere but the server's log — `error.details.oauth_error` is
`invalid_token`, and renewing the access token may help.
A 401 without it was raised about something inside the request (a wrong
password or code), and a renewal would not.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but lacking the required scope or role

NotFound.description:
Resource does not exist, or exists in another tenant. Both cases return
404 so IDs cannot be enumerated.

PaymentRequired.description:
The trial has expired and the workspace is read-only. Reads
still succeed and nothing has been deleted; writes resume on subscribing.
`error.details.access` is `read_only`; on a public-pilot deployment
(`GET /deployment` → `pilot_mode`) `error.details.reason` is also
`pilot_trial_ended` — nothing can be bought there, the way on is the
contact address.

MessageSearchTimedOut.description:
The message text search ran out of time (`service_unavailable`,
ID-07): `error.details.reason` is `search_timeout`. Nothing was
written. A narrower search — another word, a shorter date range — is
likelier to answer than the same one repeated.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the caller may retry.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the window resets.

bearerAuth.description: OAuth 2.1 access token or customer token.

x-guides.title: Authentication
x-guides.markdown:
Every request except the health checks carries a credential in the `Authorization` header. For a server-to-server integration that credential is a personal access token.

### Personal access token (server to server)

Create a token under **Settings → Integrations → Personal access tokens** in the panel, or with `POST /auth/personal-access-tokens`. The plaintext token is shown **once**; only its hash is stored, so a lost token is replaced, not recovered. Pick the narrowest scopes that do the job — a token can never be granted a scope its creator does not hold.

A personal access token is sent with HTTP Basic authentication: the username is your **account id** (`account_id` from `GET /auth/me`), the password is the token.

```bash
curl -u "$ACCOUNT_ID:$SIYAHTUS_PAT" \
  "https://api.example.com/api/v1/chats?limit=10"
```

```js
const credentials = Buffer.from(`${accountId}:${token}`).toString('base64');
const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/api/v1/chats?limit=10', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Basic ${credentials}` },
});
```

### Regions

A workspace lives in one region (`eu` or `us`) for good. A request that reaches the wrong region is answered `421 misdirected_request`; `error.details.region` names the right one.

x-guides.title: Webhook signatures
Rate limits
x-guides.markdown:
Requests are counted per credential in a sliding one-minute window.

| Caller | Default limit |
| --- | --- |
| Personal access token | 180 requests per minute per account |
| No credential | 30 requests per minute per IP address (an IPv6 /64 is one address) |

A deployment can set other values, so read the headers rather than hard-coding the numbers. A request over the limit is answered `429 too_many_requests`.

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | The ceiling for the window. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the window. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix time, in seconds, when the window resets. |
| `Retry-After` | On a `429`: seconds to wait before retrying. |

Back off for `Retry-After` seconds and retry; do not retry in a tight loop. Failed credentials count too, so a client with a bad token should stop, not keep trying.

x-guides.title: Errors
x-guides.markdown:
Every error has the same envelope. Switch on `error.type`; the HTTP status follows from it and the two never disagree.

    "type": "validation",
    "message": "limit must be between 1 and 100",
    "request_id": "01JAB2…",
    "details": { "field": "limit" }

}
